sourceEvidence.label: Session Chat contracts and primary client-storage and portable-hosting documentation

assessment.summary: Two related design opportunities are proposed: a session-scoped sealed client vault and a signed portable single-host realm appliance. Neither is implemented by this analysis.

nonNegotiables: Realm infrastructure never receives client group keys or message plaintext.
MLS, invitation, replay, approval, and encrypted Welcome-outbox state retain one atomic durability boundary.
Multi-device recovery and federation remain deferred.
assumptions: No client storage or production realm service is implemented.
No measured latency, memory, recovery-time, or availability budget was supplied.
The first deployable profile may target one Linux host with Docker Compose.

opportunities.title: Seal client secret state outside active use
opportunities.summary: Separate a bounded opaque inbox from a user-presence-gated, session-scoped secret-state vault.
opportunities.diagnosis: The design names OS-backed storage but does not yet own the unlock lifetime or define which operations remain legal while sealed.

evidence.claim: Local persistence, backups, swap, notifications, logs, and crash reports are part of the client secret boundary.
OpenMLS persistence must participate in one rollback-resistant application transaction with invitation and Welcome-outbox state.
A whole-client unlock would unnecessarily couple background opaque receipt, UI lifetime, and every session secret.

desiredInvariants: Sealed mode permits only bounded opaque-envelope receipt and non-sensitive settings.
The UI never receives vault roots, database keys, MLS secrets, or unrestricted mailbox capabilities.
Unlocking one session does not expose inactive session keys where platform and transaction constraints permit.
Encryption at rest is not treated as rollback protection.

options.title: Whole-store device wrapping
options.summary: Wrap one random store key with the strongest available OS protector and open the whole store after unlock.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Copied files become encrypted, but the whole store remains exposed while open.

tradeoffs.assessment: Narrows copied-file attacks but retains a broad unlocked scope.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test platform binding, prompts, backup restore, and locked access on every target OS.

tradeoffs.assessment: One database open and one unwrap should be the smallest candidate overhead.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure cold unlock and message-operation latency against plaintext test storage.

tradeoffs.assessment: A whole-store cache may retain more decrypted pages than a scoped design.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS with one and 1,000 expired sessions.

tradeoffs.assessment: The two-state open/closed model is comparatively simple, but loss of the device protector strands the store.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise sleep, screen-lock, crash, and protector-loss recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: Each OS needs a conformance-tested protector adapter.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Publish an adapter capability matrix and diagnostic output without secrets.

tradeoffs.assessment: One versioned encrypted store is the simplest initial format.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Round-trip fixtures across supported application versions.

residualRisks: All client secrets may be reachable while any session is open.
OS compromise and unlocked malware remain out of scope.

workPackages: Define a KeyProtector trait and whole-store lock state machine.
acceptanceCriteria: Locked operations cannot open secret state.
Copied files do not reveal canary secrets.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Delete laboratory stores and remove the adapter before any production format commitment.

options.title: Session-scoped sealed vault
options.summary: Keep a bounded opaque inbox available while a narrow core unseals only selected session state after user presence.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The design gives sealed mode an explicit capability boundary and narrows useful secret lifetime.

tradeoffs.assessment: Inactive sessions and powerful capabilities need not be available to the UI or background receiver.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Assert the locked-mode capability matrix and attempt UI-command exfiltration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Inbox import, per-session unwrap, and boundary crossings add work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark unlock, import, send, and receive latency against the whole-store baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: Per-session loading may reduce the plaintext/key working set.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak RSS and decrypted page residency under equal workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Opaque receipt continues while sealed, but lifecycle-event races and import recovery add states.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Model and crash-test every lock, wake, and concurrent-receipt transition.

tradeoffs.assessment: Platform lifecycle integration and safe lock diagnostics are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run conformance tests on supported OS and desktop environments.

tradeoffs.assessment: Opaque-inbox and per-session key schemas add format and transaction work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test upgrades, rollback rejection, and interrupted rewrapping using fixtures.

residualRisks: Malware controlling an unlocked session can capture its plaintext.
Whole-device snapshot rollback needs a separate monotonic anchor.

workPackages: Build fake and OS key protectors.
acceptanceCriteria: Sealed mode rejects every secret-bearing operation.
One session unlock does not expose inactive session keys.
MLS and Welcome state remains atomic.
migrationNotes: Start with versioned laboratory data and no production migration promise.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Fall back to the whole-store laboratory design if session scoping cannot preserve atomicity.

options.title: Dual-wrapped portable recovery
options.summary: Add an explicit Argon2id-derived portable wrapper beside the normal device-bound wrapper.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A standardized memory-hard KDF raises offline guessing cost but cannot supply passphrase entropy.

tradeoffs.assessment: Recovery adds a portable offline guessing target and continuity decisions.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model stolen recovery packages and measure KDF cost on target hardware.

tradeoffs.assessment: Argon2id intentionally consumes time and memory during recovery unlock.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Tune parameters against explicit latency and memory thresholds per platform.

tradeoffs.assessment: Memory hardness requires a large temporary allocation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak allocation and failure behavior under memory pressure.

tradeoffs.assessment: A lost device protector need not destroy recoverable state, but more paths can fail.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Restore on clean devices across application and KDF versions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Recovery export, custody, support, and incident behavior become product responsibilities.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run user and operator recovery drills with lost, weak, and corrupted phrases.

tradeoffs.assessment: New-device continuity and wrapper versioning require a dedicated protocol decision.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test wrapper rotation and visible peer key-change behavior.

residualRisks: Recovery can undermine device continuity if presented as silent restoration.

workPackages: Defer until the single-device vault passes.
Create a dedicated recovery and device-continuity ADR.
acceptanceCriteria: Recovery never silently preserves device identity.
KDF parameters meet measured target thresholds.
migrationNotes: No recovery wrapper is emitted by default.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Delete the recovery wrapper without changing the device-bound wrapper.

opportunities.recommendation: Spike session-scoped sealing with a whole-store fallback; defer portable recovery until single-device evidence and continuity UX exist.

opportunities.title: Make a realm replaceable without making it trusted for content
opportunities.summary: Package one-host realms portably and separate their stable signed identity from DNS, TLS, and any one machine.
opportunities.diagnosis: Compose is planned, but realm identity, key delegation, migration, restore classification, and session-authorized endpoint rotation are undefined.

evidence.claim: Realm operators configure service policy but must not own message keys or plaintext.
Phase 3 requires Compose plus durable CAS, crash recovery, rollback rejection, and bounded abuse evidence.
Hostname-only realm continuity would conflate transport location with stable trust and capability authority.

desiredInvariants: Realm hosts and backups never contain client plaintext or MLS group keys.
Clients accept realm endpoint changes only through a pinned, monotonic signed descriptor.
Active session endpoint rotation remains member-authenticated and right-specific.
Host loss may reduce availability but cannot silently downgrade privacy or grant membership authority.

options.title: Hostname-preserving Compose appliance
options.summary: Use digest-pinned OCI images, automatic HTTPS, explicit per-service secrets, PostgreSQL, and tested restore on one host.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It makes the planned Phase 3 deployment repeatable but does not separate realm identity from the hostname.

tradeoffs.assessment: Pinned images and scoped secrets reduce packaging mistakes; one host and hostname remain concentrated.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect images, mounts, logs, backups, and service secret access.

tradeoffs.assessment: Single-host services avoid additional network hops.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Load-test valid and abusive mailbox workloads on the minimum supported host.

tradeoffs.assessment: Proxy, services, and database share one host budget.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure idle and peak resident memory per container.

tradeoffs.assessment: Health checks, restart policy, and tested restores improve recoverability, but the host is one failure domain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Kill services and restore onto a clean machine while measuring recovery time and loss.

tradeoffs.assessment: Compose and automatic HTTPS minimize baseline operator actions after DNS setup.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a clean-host install with a first-time operator and record every manual step.

tradeoffs.assessment: OCI and database exports are portable while hostname and keys are retained.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Move the appliance across supported distributions and runtimes.

residualRisks: DNS, TLS account, database, and online keys remain one continuity boundary.
Host loss may lose opaque envelopes.

workPackages: Build production-shaped Compose and restore tests.
acceptanceCriteria: No client plaintext or group key appears server-side.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Redeploy previous compatible image digests; never downgrade incompatible database state.

options.title: Signed portable realm appliance
options.summary: Add a client-pinned offline-root realm identity, role-key delegation, monotonic descriptors, and member-authenticated session endpoint rotation.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Stable service identity becomes explicit without granting the realm content or membership authority.

tradeoffs.assessment: DNS/TLS takeover cannot silently replace a pinned realm, and online role compromise need not grant migration authority.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test forged, expired, rolled-back, cross-realm, and wrong-role descriptors and keys.

tradeoffs.assessment: Descriptor verification is infrequent and does not add a normal envelope hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure descriptor fetch/verify/cache and normal delivery latency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Clients retain a bounded descriptor chain and role keys.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Set and test strict history and descriptor-size bounds.

tradeoffs.assessment: Planned overlap and explicit disaster modes aid replacement; losing the offline root forces a new realm.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run planned and sudden replacement with clients offline across the overlap.

tradeoffs.assessment: Offline-root custody, role issuance, descriptor generations, and drain procedures add duties.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run operator drills for bootstrap, rotation, compromise, loss, and restore.

tradeoffs.assessment: Signed endpoint changes can preserve realm identity across hosts and domains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Conformance-test old/new overlap, rollback, and explicit new-realm reset.

residualRisks: A compromised offline root can redirect future realm service configuration.
Realm continuity does not rescue unbacked opaque mail or offline peers automatically.

workPackages: Model migration and peer endpoint rotation.
acceptanceCriteria: Clients reject descriptor rollback and wrong-root substitution.
Realm redirects never grant mailbox or MLS authority.
migrationNotes: Location discovery remains a hint; first trust is explicit or invitation-authenticated.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Issue a higher-generation descriptor returning to prior compatible endpoints.

options.title: Split-operator realm
options.summary: Deploy directory, sealed mailbox, and transport roles under independent failure and administrative domains.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Role separation can reduce metadata correlation and compromise scope when operators do not collude.

tradeoffs.assessment: Real operator diversity may reduce metadata correlation; co-located or colluding operators do not.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define an observer matrix and verify traffic fields at each role.

tradeoffs.assessment: More network paths and privacy transports may add latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure end-to-end invitation and message latency under realistic topology.

tradeoffs.assessment: Separate deployments duplicate proxies, runtimes, and monitoring.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure aggregate idle and peak resources across roles.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failure isolation improves, but more required roles can block a workflow.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject each single and combined role failure and record client behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Independent upgrades, incident response, clocks, and policies require coordination.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run multi-operator deployment and compromise drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: Clients and descriptors must support independent role endpoints and roots.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Move one role at a time without profile downgrade or capability confusion.

residualRisks: Collusion or one organization operating every role collapses the privacy benefit.
Small traffic volumes may remain highly correlatable.

workPackages: Defer until the signed appliance and observer matrix pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Independent placement creates a measured privacy benefit.
migrationNotes: Co-location is a different named privacy profile.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Return to co-location only through an explicit profile change.

opportunities.recommendation: Build the single-host Compose baseline, then add signed realm identity and migration before relying on hosted continuity; defer split operation.

openQuestions: Which target OS and unlock grace policy define the first vault spike?
Which monotonic anchor can reject whole-device snapshot rollback without a mandatory remote service?
What opaque-message loss and restore-time objectives define acceptable realm replacement?
How is first-use realm trust presented and recovered when the offline root is lost?
